notes.official:
*Maśśāʾ gêʾ ḥizzāyôn* is “The oracle concerning the valley of vision,” the heading formula of 13:1, 15:1 and 17:1 (overlay `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah`, extended here). ASV has “The burden of the valley of vision,” JPS 1917 “The burden concerning the Valley of Vision,” and NJPS “The ‘Valley of Vision’ Pronouncement,” with the note “Meaning of Heb. uncertain.” The sense “burden” is reported in commentary only.

*Ḥizzāyôn* is a noun of the root *ḥzh* “see,” used of prophetic vision (2 Sam 7:17; Joel 3:1 Heb.). The phrase is kept in lower case with ASV and wave ruling 7, because the Hebrew does not mark it as a place name and the valley is not identified. The same phrase recurs at 22:5 and is printed the same way there. Verses 9–11 show that the city addressed is Jerusalem.

*Mah-lāḵ ʾēp̄ôʾ* “What ails you now” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “What can have happened to you”). The second-person forms are feminine singular, addressed to the city. NJPS notes that public mourning took place on the flat roofs, as at 15:3, where the book also prints “housetops.”

notes.official:
*Miqqešeṯ ʾussārû* is literally “from the bow they were bound.” ASV takes *min* as marking the agent and the bow as the archers who bind: “they were bound by the archers.” JPS 1917 (“Without the bow they are bound”) and NJPS (“Taken captive without their bows,” note “Meaning of Heb. uncertain”) take *min* as privative, so that the officers surrendered without using their weapons. Both uses of *min* are attested. The line keeps the ASV construal, which reads the verse as a single scene of capture, and reports the privative reading here (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`).

*Qᵉṣînayiḵ* is “your rulers” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “your officers”). The verb *ʾsr* “bind” occurs twice, and the English repeats “bound,” as the Hebrew does.

paragraphs.translit: kol-qəṣīnayik nādədū-yaḥad miqqešet ʾussārū kol-nimṣāʾayik ʾussərū yaḥdāw mērāḥōq bārāḥū

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֛רְתִּי שְׁע֥וּ מִנִּ֖י אֲמָרֵ֣ר בַּבֶּ֑כִי אַל־תָּאִ֣יצוּ לְנַֽחֲמֵ֔נִי עַל־שֹׁ֖ד בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: Therefore I said: “Look away from me, I will weep bitterly; do not labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֛רְתִּי שְׁע֥וּ מִנִּ֖י אֲמָרֵ֣ר בַּבֶּ֑כִי אַל־תָּאִ֣יצוּ לְנַֽחֲמֵ֔נִי עַל־שֹׁ֖ד בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃

notes.official:
*ʿAl-šōḏ baṯ-ʿammî* “for the destruction of the daughter of my people” follows ASV and JPS 1917. *Baṯ-ʿammî* is a genitive of apposition, “the daughter who is my people,” formed like *baṯ-ṣiyyôn* “the daughter of Zion” (1:8). NJPS renders the sense as “my poor people” and gives the literal meaning in a note, “the young woman, my people.” The phrase is frequent in Jeremiah and Lamentations (Jer 4:11; 8:19, 21; Lam 2:11). The literal form is kept so that the personified people stays visible, and the decision is recorded in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`.

*ʿAl-kēn ʾāmartî* is past, “Therefore I said,” with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS reads the perfect as present, “That is why I say.” *Šᵉʿû minnî* “Look away from me” and *ʾal-tāʾîṣû* “do not labor” (literally “do not press, hurry”; NJPS “Press not”) follow ASV. The prophet's words are in quotation marks, as in JPS 1917 and NJPS.

paragraphs.translit: ʿal-kēn ʾāmartī šəʿū minnī ʾămārēr babbekī ʾal-tāʾīṣū lənaḥămēnī ʿal-šōd bat-ʿammī

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י יוֹם֩ מְהוּמָ֨ה וּמְבוּסָ֜ה וּמְבוּכָ֗ה לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּגֵ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מְקַרְקַ֥ר קִ֖ר וְשׁ֥וֹעַ אֶל־הָהָֽר׃

i18n.en: For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of tumult, and of treading down, and of perplexity, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the wall, and a crying to the mountain.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י יוֹם֩ מְהוּמָ֨ה וּמְבוּסָ֜ה וּמְבוּכָ֗ה לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּגֵ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מְקַרְקַ֥ר קִ֖ר וְשׁ֥וֹעַ אֶל־הָהָֽר׃

notes.official:
*Kî yôm … laʾḏōnāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is rendered as possession, “For the Lord YHWH of hosts has a day of tumult,” with NJPS (“For my Lord GOD of Hosts had a day”). NRSV is recalled as reading the same way; this was not verified. ASV and JPS 1917 read “a day … from the Lord.” The preposition *lᵉ* after *yôm* is the construction of 2:12, *kî yôm laYHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ*, which the stable chapter prints as “there is a day of YHWH of hosts.” The possessive reading keeps the two verses concordant and does not give *lᵉ* the sense “from,” which it rarely has. The change from the draft is recorded in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`.

*Mᵉhûmāh ûmᵉḇûsāh ûmᵉḇûḵāh* is an alliterative triad, “tumult, and treading down, and perplexity.” JPS 1917 has “trouble,” ASV “discomfiture,” and NJPS “tumult” for the first noun.

*Mᵉqarqar qir wᵉšôaʿ ʾel-hāhār* is a word-play that the versions read in two ways. ASV takes the words as common nouns: *qir* “wall,” with the Pilpel of *qrr* “tear down,” and *šôaʿ* “cry for help”: “a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains.” JPS 1917 (“Kir shouting, and Shoa at the mount”) and NJPS (“Kir raged in the Valley of Vision, / And Shoa on the hill”) take Kir and Shoa as peoples. NJPS notes “Meaning of Heb. uncertain” and cites Kir at 2 Kgs 16:9 and Amos 1:5; 9:7, and Shoa at Ezek 23:23. Kir does appear in 22:6. The line keeps the common-noun sense of ASV, but in the singular, as MT has it (“the wall,” “the mountain”).

paragraphs.translit: kī yōm məhūmāh ūməbūsāh ūməbūkāh laʾdōnāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt bəgēʾ ḥizzāyōn məqarqar qir wəšōaʿ ʾel-hāhār

paragraphs.text: וְעֵילָם֙ נָשָׂ֣א אַשְׁפָּ֔ה בְּרֶ֥כֶב אָדָ֖ם פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וְקִ֥יר עֵרָ֖ה מָגֵֽן׃

i18n.en: And Elam bore the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.
i18n.he: וְעֵילָם֙ נָשָׂ֣א אַשְׁפָּ֔ה בְּרֶ֥כֶב אָדָ֖ם פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וְקִ֥יר עֵרָ֖ה מָגֵֽן׃

notes.official:
*Bᵉreḵeḇ ʾāḏām pārāšîm* is asyndetic: “with chariotry of men, horsemen.” ASV supplies “[and]” in brackets; the line supplies “and” as well. JPS 1917 reads the second noun as apposition (“with troops of men, even horsemen”), and NJPS reads the phrase as one unit (“In troops of mounted men”). *ʾĀḏām* here is the crews or troops of an army, not humankind in general. Wave ruling 13 keeps “men” for nouns that denote a specific body of fighting men, so the gender-neutral rule of `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah` does not apply.

Elam lay east of Babylonia. Kir is the place to which Aram was deported (2 Kgs 16:9; Amos 1:5; 9:7), not Kir of Moab (15:1). *ʿĒrāh māḡēn* “uncovered the shield” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “bared the shield”). It refers to removing the shield's cover for battle.

paragraphs.translit: wəʿēlām nāśāʾ ʾašpāh bərekeb ʾādām pārāšīm wəqīr ʿērāh māgēn

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י מִבְחַר־עֲמָקַ֖יִךְ מָ֣לְאוּ רָ֑כֶב וְהַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים שֹׁ֖ת שָׁ֥תוּ הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass that your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.
i18n.he: וַיְהִ֥י מִבְחַר־עֲמָקַ֖יִךְ מָ֣לְאוּ רָ֑כֶב וְהַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים שֹׁ֖ת שָׁ֥תוּ הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃

notes.official: *Mibḥar-ʿămāqayiḵ* “your choicest valleys” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “your choicest lowlands”). *Šōṯ šāṯû haššāʿrāh* is an infinitive absolute with its finite verb, “they set themselves firmly at the gate” (ASV “set themselves in array”). JPS 1917 subordinates the verse to v. 8 (“when thy choicest valleys were full”). NJPS moves “Judah's” up from v. 8 and explains the gate as the upper course of the Valley of Elah. The line keeps ASV's independent clause.

paragraphs.translit: wayhī mibḥar-ʿămāqayik māləʾū rākeb wəhappārāšīm šōt šātū haššāʿrāh

paragraphs.text: וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל־נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר׃

i18n.en: And he took away the covering of Judah; and you looked in that day to the armor of the house of the forest.
i18n.he: וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל־נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר׃

notes.official:
*Wayᵉḡal ʾēṯ māsaḵ yᵉhûḏāh* has no expressed subject. ASV supplies “he took away the covering of Judah,” and the line follows it; the subject may be YHWH or the enemy. JPS 1917 renders the active verb as a passive (“the covering of Judah was laid bare”), and NJPS (“And pressed beyond its screen”) explains the screen as the fortress Azekah. *Māsāḵ* is a covering or screen, the word for the tabernacle screen (Exod 26:36). The line keeps the general sense, “covering” (`lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`).

*Bêṯ hayyaʿar* is “the house of the forest,” Solomon's “house of the forest of Lebanon” (1 Kgs 7:2), where the gold shields were kept (1 Kgs 10:17). ASV prints the name in lower case, and the line follows it. NJPS has “the Forest House” and cites 1 Kgs 7:2–5 and 10:16–17.

paragraphs.translit: waygal ʾēt māsak yəhūdāh wattabbēṭ bayyōm hahūʾ ʾel-nešeq bēt hayyāʿar

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֨ת בְּקִיעֵ֧י עִיר־דָּוִ֛ד רְאִיתֶ֖ם כִּי־רָ֑בּוּ וַֽתְּקַבְּצ֔וּ אֶת־מֵ֥י הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And you saw the breaches of the city of David, that they were many; and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
i18n.he: וְאֵ֨ת בְּקִיעֵ֧י עִיר־דָּוִ֛ד רְאִיתֶ֖ם כִּי־רָ֑בּוּ וַֽתְּקַבְּצ֔וּ אֶת־מֵ֥י הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃

notes.official: Verses 9–11 describe the defensive work in Jerusalem: the breaches in the wall, the houses pulled down to strengthen it, and the gathering of water. Hezekiah's similar measures before the Assyrian siege are reported at 2 Kgs 20:20 and 2 Chr 32:3–5, 30. The line follows ASV. NJPS notes that the clause about the lower pool “would read well after the prose part of v. 11a.”

paragraphs.translit: wəʾēt bəqīʿē ʿīr-dāwid rəʾītem kī-rābbū wattəqabbəṣū ʾet-mē habbərēkāh hattaḥtōnāh

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־בָּתֵּ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם וַתִּתְֿצוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים לְבַצֵּ֖ר הַחוֹמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.
i18n.he: וְאֶת־בָּתֵּ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם וַתִּתְֿצוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים לְבַצֵּ֖ר הַחוֹמָֽה׃

paragraphs.translit: wəʾet-bāttē yərūšālim səpartem wattittəṣū habbāttīm ləbaṣṣēr haḥōmāh

paragraphs.text: וּמִקְוָ֣ה ׀ עֲשִׂיתֶ֗ם בֵּ֚ין הַחֹ֣מֹתַ֔יִם לְמֵ֖י הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הַיְשָׁנָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הִבַּטְתֶּם֙ אֶל־עֹשֶׂ֔יהָ וְיֹצְרָ֥הּ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לֹ֥א רְאִיתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool; but you did not look to the one who made it, nor did you see the one who formed it long ago.
i18n.he: וּמִקְוָ֣ה ׀ עֲשִׂיתֶ֗ם בֵּ֚ין הַחֹ֣מֹתַ֔יִם לְמֵ֖י הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הַיְשָׁנָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הִבַּטְתֶּם֙ אֶל־עֹשֶׂ֔יהָ וְיֹצְרָ֥הּ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לֹ֥א רְאִיתֶֽם׃

notes.official:
*ʿŌśêhā … wᵉyōṣᵉrāh* is rendered “the one who made it … the one who formed it long ago.” The verbs are ʿāśāh “make” (central `asah`) and yāṣar “form” (central `yatsar`). The suffixed participle of yāṣar with God as subject keeps its verbal force, under overlay `yotser-potter-clay-image-isaiah`, and the parallel ʿōśêhā is matched to it. ʿŌśêhā is plural in form. The vowel before the suffix is that of the plural noun, as in Job 35:10 and Ps 149:2, where the participle of ʿśh refers to God. The English uses the singular, as ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS do. The stable chapters print ʿōśēhû as “its maker” (29:16) and ʿōśayiḵ as “your Maker” (54:5). Here the verbal phrase is kept, so that the two halves of the line stay parallel.

The feminine suffix -hā has no stated antecedent. It may be the city or the reservoir, or the event as a whole, as ASV takes it: “him that had done this … him that purposed it long ago.” NJPS has “Him who planned it … Him who designed it long before.” *Yāṣar* “form” is used of a plan formed in advance at 37:26 (“that I have formed it of ancient times,” with the same verb); 37:26 has not yet been translated. The line keeps the concrete verbs, which also cover the planning sense, and leaves the referent open.

*Hibbaṭtem ʾel-* “look to” and *rᵉʾîṯem* “see” are the pair of 5:12 (“they do not regard … nor have they seen”), with *hibbîṭ ʾel* in its idiomatic sense “look to, rely on.” *Miqwāh* is “a reservoir” (ASV); JPS 1917 and NJPS have “a basin.” *Bên haḥōmōṯayim* “between the two walls” recurs at 2 Kgs 25:4.

paragraphs.translit: ūmiqwāh | ʿăśītem bēn haḥōmōtayim ləmē habbərēkāh hayšānāh wəlōʾ hibbaṭtem ʾel-ʿōśehā wəyōṣərāh mērāḥōq lōʾ rəʾītem

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לִבְכִי֙ וּלְמִסְפֵּ֔ד וּלְקָרְחָ֖ה וְלַחֲגֹ֥ר שָֽׂק׃

i18n.en: And in that day the Lord YHWH of hosts called to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth;
i18n.he: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לִבְכִי֙ וּלְמִסְפֵּ֔ד וּלְקָרְחָ֖ה וְלַחֲגֹ֥ר שָֽׂק׃

notes.official: *Qorḥāh* “baldness” is the mourning rite of 15:2 and 3:24, and *ḥăḡōr śaq* “girding with sackcloth” the rite of 15:3, so the lament vocabulary of the Moab oracles recurs here. ASV and JPS 1917 have “baldness,” and NJPS “tonsuring.”

paragraphs.translit: wayyiqrāʾ ʾădōnāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt bayyōm hahūʾ libkī ūləmispēd ūləqorḥāh wəlaḥăgōr śāq

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֗ה הָרֹ֤ג ׀ בָּקָר֙ וְשָׁחֹ֣ט צֹ֔אן אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר וְשָׁת֣וֹת יָ֑יִן אָכ֣וֹל וְשָׁת֔וֹ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר נָמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: and behold, joy and gladness, slaying oxen and slaughtering sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die.”
i18n.he: וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֗ה הָרֹ֤ג ׀ בָּקָר֙ וְשָׁחֹ֣ט צֹ֔אן אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר וְשָׁת֣וֹת יָ֑יִן אָכ֣וֹל וְשָׁת֔וֹ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר נָמֽוּת׃

notes.official:
*ʾĀḵôl wᵉšāṯô kî māḥār nāmûṯ* is quoted, in Greek, at 1 Cor 15:32, which ASV renders “let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die.” The Hebrew uses two infinitives absolute with a cohortative or imperatival sense, followed by an imperfect. ASV and JPS 1917 supply a cohortative and a future: “let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die.” NJPS has “Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!” The line follows ASV. The wording of the LXX at Isa 22:13 was not verified, so the commentary does not say whether Paul quotes it word for word.

The preceding infinitives absolute (*hārōḡ … wᵉšāḥōṭ … ʾāḵōl … wᵉšāṯôṯ*) are rendered as gerunds, “slaying … slaughtering … eating … drinking,” as in ASV. The revelers' words are in quotation marks, as in JPS 1917 and NJPS. *Wᵉhinnēh* “and behold” sets the feast against the call to mourning in v. 12.

paragraphs.translit: wəhinnēh | śāśōn wəśimḥāh hārōg | bāqār wəšāḥōṭ ṣōʾn ʾākōl bāśār wəšātōt yāyin ʾākōl wəšātō kī māḥār nāmūt

paragraphs.text: וְנִגְלָ֥ה בְאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־יְ֠כֻפַּר הֶעָוֺ֨ן הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ עַד־תְּמֻת֔וּן אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And YHWH of hosts revealed himself in my ears: Surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die, says the Lord YHWH of hosts.
i18n.he: וְנִגְלָ֥ה בְאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־יְ֠כֻפַּר הֶעָוֺ֨ן הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ עַד־תְּמֻת֔וּן אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (פ)

notes.official:
*ʾIm-yᵉḵuppar heʿāwōn hazzeh lāḵem* is an oath formula. *ʾIm* with an unexpressed curse is a strong negative: “Surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you.” *Yᵉḵuppar* is the Pual of *kpr*, rendered “atoned for” as at 6:7 and 27:9 (overlay `kupar-atonement-isaiah`, extended here). ASV and NJPS have “forgiven,” and JPS 1917 “expiated.” *ʿĀwōn* is “iniquity” (central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`). The Targum is recalled as reading “until you die the second death,” a phrase also found in Rev 2:11 and 20:6. This was not verified against an edition.

*Wᵉniḡlāh bᵉʾoznāy YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is “And YHWH of hosts revealed himself in my ears,” with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS. The Niphal of *glh* can also be read as a passive with YHWH as agent, “it was revealed in my ears by YHWH of hosts,” which is close to 5:9, “In my ears YHWH of hosts says.” The divine words follow the colon without quotation marks, under the book's messenger-formula style (`title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wəniglāh bəʾoznāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt ʾim-yəkuppar heʿāwōn hazzeh lākem ʿad-təmutūn ʾāmar ʾădōnāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt (p)

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: Thus says the Lord YHWH of hosts: Go, get you to this treasurer, to Shebna, who is over the house:
i18n.he: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הַבָּֽיִת׃

notes.official:
*Hassōḵēn hazzeh* “this treasurer” follows ASV. JPS 1917 and NJPS have “steward.” *Sōḵēn* occurs only here as the title of an office; the feminine *sōḵeneṯ* is the king's attendant in 1 Kgs 1:2, 4. Cognates in Ugaritic and Phoenician (*skn*, a prefect or governor) point to a high administrative officer rather than a keeper of the treasury (HALOT; recalled, not verified). “Treasurer” is kept as the public-domain baseline, and “steward” is recorded as the closer gloss (`lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`). *ʾĂšer ʿal-habbāyiṯ* “who is over the house” is the title of the palace chief (1 Kgs 4:6; 18:3; 2 Kgs 18:18; NJPS “in charge of the palace”).

In 36:3 and 2 Kgs 18:18, Eliakim son of Hilkiah is “over the house” and Shebna is “the scribe,” which agrees with the transfer of office announced in vv. 19–22. A rock-cut tomb inscription from Silwan names an official “…yahu who is over the house.” The identification of that official with Shebna(yahu) is often proposed but uncertain (N. Avigad, IEJ 3, 1953; recalled).

*Lek-bōʾ ʾel … ʿal-šeḇnāʾ* is “Go, get you to … to Shebna”; *ʿal* is used here in the sense of *ʾel*. ASV supplies “[and say]” before v. 16. The line does not supply it, and the speech of vv. 16–25 follows without quotation marks.

paragraphs.translit: kōh ʾāmar ʾădōnāy YHWH ṣəbāʾōt lek-bōʾ ʾel-hassōkēn hazzeh ʿal-šebnāʾ ʾăšer ʿal-habbāyit

paragraphs.text: מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹה֙ וּמִ֣י לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה כִּֽי־חָצַ֧בְתָּ לְּךָ֛ פֹּ֖ה קָ֑בֶר חֹצְבִ֤י מָרוֹם֙ קִבְר֔וֹ חֹקְקִ֥י בַסֶּ֖לַע מִשְׁכָּ֥ן לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here — hewing out his tomb on high, carving a dwelling for himself in the rock?
i18n.he: מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹה֙ וּמִ֣י לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה כִּֽי־חָצַ֧בְתָּ לְּךָ֛ פֹּ֖ה קָ֑בֶר חֹצְבִ֤י מָרוֹם֙ קִבְר֔וֹ חֹקְקִ֥י בַסֶּ֖לַע מִשְׁכָּ֥ן לֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *Ḥōṣᵉḇî mārôm qiḇrô ḥōqᵉqî ḇassela miškān lô* changes from the second person to the third: “hewing out his tomb on high, carving a dwelling for himself in the rock.” The participles end in the old connecting vowel *-î*, and the clause can be read as an exclamation about Shebna. The line keeps the third person with ASV alone (“hewing him out a sepulchre on high”). JPS 1917 and NJPS both convert to the second person: JPS 1917 has “Thou that hewest thee out a sepulchre on high, And gravest a habitation for thyself in the rock,” and NJPS has “O you who have hewn your tomb on high,” noting “Heb. ‘his,’ ‘himself.’” *Qeḇer* is “tomb” (JPS 1917 and ASV have “sepulchre”). The opening *mah-lᵉḵā pōh ûmî lᵉḵā pōh* “What have you here, and whom have you here” follows JPS 1917 and NJPS (ASV “What doest thou here?”). It questions Shebna's right to a family tomb in Jerusalem.

paragraphs.translit: mah-ləkā pōh ūmī ləkā pōh kī-ḥāṣabtā ləkā pōh qāber ḥōṣəbī mārōm qibrō ḥōqəqī basselaʿ miškān lō

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְטַלְטֶלְךָ֔ טַלְטֵלָ֖ה גָּ֑בֶר וְעֹטְךָ֖ עָטֹֽה׃

i18n.en: Behold, YHWH will hurl you away violently, like a strong man; and he will wrap you up closely.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְטַלְטֶלְךָ֔ טַלְטֵלָ֖ה גָּ֑בֶר וְעֹטְךָ֖ עָטֹֽה׃

notes.official:
*Mᵉṭalṭelᵉḵā ṭalṭēlāh gāḇer* combines a participle and a cognate noun of *ṭûl* “hurl” (Pilpel) with the noun *geḇer* “man, strong man.” ASV reads *gāḇer* as a comparison, “like a [strong] man,” and the line follows it without the brackets. JPS 1917 reads a genitive, “with a man's throw.” NJPS reads a vocative, “Severely, fellow,” and notes that an emendation yields “as a garment is shaken out.”

*Wᵉʿōṭᵉḵā ʿāṭōh* “and he will wrap you up closely” follows ASV. NJPS has “and then wrap you around Himself,” with the note “I.e., and walk off with you; cf. Jer. 43.12,” where the same verb describes wrapping oneself in a garment. A second verb *ʿṭh*, “grasp,” is proposed in some lexica (HALOT; recalled, not verified). That sense would give “grasp you firmly,” and JPS 1917 has “wind thee round and round.” The line keeps ASV, whose rendering continues into the winding image of v. 18.

paragraphs.translit: hinnēh YHWH məṭalṭeləkā ṭalṭēlāh gāber wəʿōṭəkā ʿāṭōh

paragraphs.text: צָנ֤וֹף יִצְנָפְךָ֙ צְנֵפָ֔ה כַּדּ֕וּר אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדָ֑יִם שָׁ֣מָּה תָמ֗וּת וְשָׁ֙מָּה֙ מַרְכְּב֣וֹת כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ קְל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: He will surely wind you round and round, like a ball, into a wide land; there you shall die, and there shall be the chariots of your glory, O shame of your lord's house.
i18n.he: צָנ֤וֹף יִצְנָפְךָ֙ צְנֵפָ֔ה כַּדּ֕וּר אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדָ֑יִם שָׁ֣מָּה תָמ֗וּת וְשָׁ֙מָּה֙ מַרְכְּב֣וֹת כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ קְל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

notes.official:
*Ṣānôp̄ yiṣnāp̄ᵉḵā ṣᵉnēp̄āh kaddûr* is literally “he will wind you tightly, a winding, like a ball.” *Ṣnp* is the verb for winding a turban (Lev 16:4), and NJPS reads “He will wind you about Him as a headdress, a turban,” noting an emendation. The line has “He will surely wind you round and round, like a ball,” the ASV wording without its supplied “[and toss thee].” *ʾEreṣ raḥăḇaṯ yāḏāyim* “a wide land” (literally “broad on both hands,” as in Gen 34:21) is rendered under the central `eretz` entry (ASV “a large country”; NJPS “a broad land”).

*Markᵉḇôṯ kᵉḇôḏeḵā* “the chariots of your glory” keeps “glory” for *kāḇôḏ* under wave ruling 2, which makes the rendering strict for non-divine uses too. The decision for 22:18, 23 and 24 is recorded in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`. ASV and JPS 1917 have the same wording. NJPS has “the chariots bearing your body” and notes an emendation yielding “abode … of your body.” The phrase refers to the state chariots of a high official (cf. 2 Sam 15:1).

*Qᵉlôn bêṯ ʾăḏōneyḵā* is “O shame of your lord's house.” *ʾĂḏōneyḵā* is plural in form, the usual honorific for a master, and here refers to the king. It is lower case, with ASV; NJPS has “your master's house.” The articular divine title of `ha-adon-articular-title-isaiah` does not apply.

paragraphs.translit: ṣānōp yiṣnāpəkā ṣənēpāh kaddūr ʾel-ʾereṣ raḥăbat yādāyim šāmmāh tāmūt wəšāmmāh markəbōt kəbōdekā qəlōn bēt ʾădōnekā

paragraphs.text: וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And I will thrust you from your office, and from your station you shall be pulled down.
i18n.he: וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ׃

notes.official: *Wahăḏap̄tîḵā mimmaṣṣāḇeḵā ûmimmaʿămāḏᵉḵā yehersᵉḵā* changes from the first person (“I will thrust you”) to the third (“he will pull you down”). The third-person verb can be read with an indefinite subject, and ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render it as a passive: “from your station you shall be pulled down.” The line follows them. The MT person is reported here and in `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`. *Maṣṣāḇ* is “office” (ASV; JPS 1917 “post”), and *maʿămāḏ* “station.”

paragraphs.translit: wahădaptīkā mimmaṣṣābekā ūmimmaʿămādəkā yehersekā

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah;
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

notes.official: *ʿAḇdî* “my servant” is the title given to Isaiah in 20:3 and to David elsewhere. It marks a commissioned agent of YHWH and is not the figure governed by `eved-servant-identity-isaiah` in chapters 40–55. Eliakim son of Hilkiah is the official “over the house” in 36:3, 22 and 2 Kgs 18:18.

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh bayyōm hahūʾ wəqārāʾtī ləʿabdī ləʾelyāqīm ben-ḥilqiyyāhū

paragraphs.text: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתִּ֣יו כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ אֲחַזְּקֶ֔נּוּ וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְאָ֛ב לְיוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּלְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your girdle, and I will commit your government into his hand; and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
i18n.he: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתִּ֣יו כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ אֲחַזְּקֶ֔נּוּ וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְאָ֛ב לְיוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּלְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃

notes.official:
The investiture vocabulary follows ASV (`lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`). *Kuttōneṯ* is “robe” (ASV, JPS 1917). NJPS has “tunic,” which is the garment's form. *ʾAḇnēṭ* is the sash of priestly dress (Exod 28:4, 39; Lev 8:7). ASV and JPS 1917 render it “girdle,” which the stable chapters also use for *ʾēzôr* (11:5) and *ḥăḡôrāh* (3:24); NJPS has “sash.” *ʾĂḥazzᵉqennû* is “strengthen him” (ASV). JPS 1917 has “bind him,” and NJPS “gird him.”

*Memšalṯᵉḵā* is “your government” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “your authority”). The noun is *memšālāh* “rule, dominion” (cf. 39:2, which has not yet been translated). The stable 9:5 uses the same English word, “government,” for a different noun, *miśrāh*. The two passages share the image of authority laid on the shoulder (22:22; 9:5), and the shared English word is kept. The Hebrew difference is stated here.

*Wᵉhāyāh lᵉʾāḇ* “and he shall be a father” uses “father” as a title of a senior official, as in Gen 45:8 (“a father to Pharaoh”). *Lᵉyôšēḇ yᵉrûšālayim* is a singular collective, rendered “the inhabitants.” NJPS 1985 renders *bêṯ yᵉhûḏāh* as “the men of Judah”; the line keeps the literal “the house of Judah,” with ASV and JPS 1917.

paragraphs.translit: wəhilbaštīw kuttāntekā wəʾabnēṭəkā ʾăḥazzəqennū ūmemšaltəkā ʾettēn bəyādō wəhāyāh ləʾāb ləyōšēb yərūšālim ūləbēt yəhūdāh

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתִּ֛י מַפְתֵּ֥חַ בֵּית־דָּוִ֖ד עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וּפָתַח֙ וְאֵ֣ין סֹגֵ֔ר וְסָגַ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין פֹּתֵֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder; and he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
i18n.he: וְנָתַתִּ֛י מַפְתֵּ֥חַ בֵּית־דָּוִ֖ד עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וּפָתַח֙ וְאֵ֣ין סֹגֵ֔ר וְסָגַ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין פֹּתֵֽחַ׃

notes.official:
*Maptēaḥ bêṯ-dāwiḏ* is “the key of the house of David,” in the singular, with ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “the keys of David's palace”). *Maptēaḥ* is a key (Judg 3:25; 1 Chr 9:27). The phrase *ʿal-šiḵmô* “upon his shoulder” is the wording of 9:5, “the government has come upon his shoulder.” A key carried on the shoulder is usually explained as a large wooden key or as a badge of office. The central entry on Gen 48:22 *šᵉḵem* (`shekhem-achad-polysemy-historical-redactional-crux`) mentions this verse only in its rationale and is not applied.

*Ûp̄āṯaḥ wᵉʾên sōḡēr wᵉsāḡar wᵉʾên pōṯēaḥ* “he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open” states the steward's full control of access to the palace.

Rev 3:7 quotes the line and applies it to the risen Christ: “he that hath the key of David, he that openeth and none shall shut, and that shutteth and none openeth” (ASV). The keys and the binding and loosing of Matt 16:19 are often compared. Whether Rev 3:7 follows the Hebrew or the LXX of Isa 22:22 was not verified. The parallels are reported as reception history; the line translates the Hebrew.

paragraphs.translit: wənātattī maptēaḥ bēt-dāwid ʿal-šikmō ūpātaḥ wəʾēn sōgēr wəsāgar wəʾēn pōtēaḥ

paragraphs.text: וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו יָתֵ֖ד בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְהָיָ֛ה לְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד לְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place; and he shall be a throne of glory for his father's house.
i18n.he: וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו יָתֵ֖ד בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְהָיָ֛ה לְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד לְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃

notes.official:
*Ûṯᵉqaʿtîw yāṯēḏ* is “I will fasten him as a peg.” *Tāqaʿ yāṯēḏ* is the idiom for driving a tent peg (Judg 4:21). The same noun is a peg in a wall from which vessels hang (Ezek 15:3), which is the picture of v. 24. ASV has “a nail,” JPS 1917 “a peg,” and NJPS “a peg.” The stable 54:2 prints the tent sense as “stakes.” Overlay `yated-peg-stake-isaiah` fixes “peg” here and at 22:25, where the object is driven and hung with vessels, and keeps “stake” for tent pegs.

*Bᵉmāqôm neʾĕmān* “in a sure place” uses the Niphal of *ʾmn* “be firm, reliable.” The same form is used of David's house in 2 Sam 7:16 (*wᵉneʾman bêṯᵉḵā*), and the root is played on in Isa 7:9.

*Kissēʾ ḵāḇôḏ* is “a throne of glory,” with ASV, under wave ruling 2. JPS 1917 has “a throne of honour” and NJPS “a seat of honor.” The same phrase in 1 Sam 2:8 is “the throne of glory” in ASV. NJPS moves 23b before 23a and notes an emendation of *ʾāḇîw* “his father's” to “his master's” (cf. v. 18).

paragraphs.translit: ūtəqaʿtīw yātēd bəmāqōm neʾĕmān wəhāyāh ləkissēʾ kābōd ləbēt ʾābīw

paragraphs.text: וְתָל֨וּ עָלָ֜יו כֹּ֣ל ׀ כְּב֣וֹד בֵּית־אָבִ֗יו הַצֶּֽאֱצָאִים֙ וְהַצְּפִע֔וֹת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַקָּטָ֑ן מִכְּלֵי֙ הָֽאַגָּנ֔וֹת וְעַ֖ד כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּבָלִֽים׃

i18n.en: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the vessels of cups even to all the vessels of flagons.
i18n.he: וְתָל֨וּ עָלָ֜יו כֹּ֣ל ׀ כְּב֣וֹד בֵּית־אָבִ֗יו הַצֶּֽאֱצָאִים֙ וְהַצְּפִע֔וֹת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַקָּטָ֑ן מִכְּלֵי֙ הָֽאַגָּנ֔וֹת וְעַ֖ד כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּבָלִֽים׃

notes.official:
*Kōl kᵉḇôḏ bêṯ-ʾāḇîw* is “all the glory of his father's house,” with ASV and JPS 1917, under wave ruling 2 (`lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`). NJPS has “all the substance,” the sense of weight carried by the root *kbd*. The image is of a peg weighed down by what is hung on it.

*Haṣṣeʾĕṣāʾîm wᵉhaṣṣᵉp̄iʿôṯ* is “the offspring and the issue” (ASV, JPS 1917). *Ṣeʾĕṣāʾîm* is “offspring” in the stable 44:3, 48:19 and 65:23. At 42:5 it is what the earth brings forth (“what comes forth from it”), which is the basis of NJPS “the sprouts and the leaves.” *Ṣᵉp̄iʿôṯ* occurs only here, and NJPS notes “Meaning of Heb. uncertain.”

*ʾAggānôṯ* is “cups” (ASV); the word is a bowl or basin in Exod 24:6 and NJPS has “bowls.” *Nᵉḇālîm* is “flagons” (ASV; NJPS “jars”). It is *nēḇel* II, a jar or skin bottle (1 Sam 1:24; Jer 13:12), a homonym of *nēḇel* I “harp,” which is printed as “harp” at 5:12 and 14:11. The line keeps the repeated *kᵉlê* (“the vessels of cups … the vessels of flagons”) with JPS 1917; ASV omits it.

i18n.en: In that day, says YHWH of hosts, the peg that was fastened in a sure place shall give way; and it shall be cut down and fall, and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off; for YHWH has spoken.

notes.official:
*Hayyāṯēḏ hattᵉqûʿāh bᵉmāqôm neʾĕmān* is “the peg that was fastened in a sure place,” as in 22:23 (`yated-peg-stake-isaiah`; ASV “nail,” JPS 1917 and NJPS “peg”). The verse does not say whose fall it announces. The immediate context points to Eliakim and the weight of his family hung on him (vv. 23–24). NJPS notes that the verse “apparently continues v. 19,” which would make it a final word on Shebna. The line does not decide.

*Hammaśśāʾ ʾăšer-ʿālehā* is “the burden that was upon it,” with ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “the weight it supports”). This is *maśśāʾ* I, a load, from *nśʾ* “lift, carry.” The heading of 22:1 uses *maśśāʾ* II, rendered “oracle.” The scope note in `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah` (extended here) confirms that its rule for headings does not reach this verse. The chapter closes on the same consonants as its heading, and the play is lost in English. The stable 9:3, 10:27 and 14:25 also print “burden,” but for a different noun, *sōḇel*.

*Tāmûš* “shall give way” follows ASV and JPS 1917. *Wᵉniḡdᵉʿāh* is “cut down” (ASV “hewn down”). *Nᵉʾum YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is “says YHWH of hosts.” *Kî YHWH dibbēr* “for YHWH has spoken” is a closing formula, a shorter form of 1:20 “for the mouth of YHWH has spoken.”
